title: AML Structuring Policy
text: AML Structuring Policy (POL-001) - Purpose and Scope: This policy defines how the bank detects and escalates structuring, the practice of splitting cash transactions into smaller amounts to avoid reporting thresholds. It applies to all savings, current and loan accounts across retail, SME and corporate segments.

title: AML Structuring Policy
text: AML Structuring Policy (POL-001) - Definitions: Structuring means three or more cash deposits by the same account within a rolling 7-day window, each between INR 9,00,000 and INR 9,99,999, where the combined value exceeds INR 10,00,000. The reporting threshold refers to the INR 10,00,000 cash transaction reporting limit.

title: AML Structuring Policy
text: AML Structuring Policy (POL-001) - Detection Rules: Rule STR-R1: three or more CASH_DEPOSIT transactions of INR 9,00,000 to 9,99,999 in 7 days. Rule STR-R2: the same pattern across multiple accounts of one customer, aggregated at customer level. Alerts are scored High when the deposits fall within 48 hours, and Medium otherwise.

title: AML Structuring Policy
text: AML Structuring Policy (POL-001) - Escalation Workflow: Level 1 analyst reviews within 1 business day. Confirmed or unresolved alerts go to the AML Compliance Officer within 2 business days. The Principal Officer decides on filing a Suspicious Transaction Report (STR), which must be filed within 7 working days of concluding suspicion.

title: AML Structuring Policy
text: AML Structuring Policy (POL-001) - Evidence Required: The case file must contain the transaction list with IDs and timestamps, the account and customer profile, KYC status, average monthly inflow compared with deposited amounts, and the analyst's written rationale. Conclusions without transaction-level evidence are not accepted for closure.

title: AML Structuring Policy
text: AML Structuring Policy (POL-001) - Confidentiality: Staff must not inform the customer that an alert or STR exists (no tipping-off). Case notes are restricted to the AML team and Internal Audit.

title: AML Structuring Policy
text: AML Structuring Policy (POL-001) - Record Retention: Alerts, case files and STR copies are retained for at least 5 years from case closure.

title: High-Risk Jurisdiction Transfers
text: High-Risk Jurisdiction Transfers (POL-002) - Purpose and Scope: This policy governs outgoing and incoming transfers involving counterparties in jurisdictions the bank classifies as high risk. It covers RTGS, NEFT, IMPS and card cross-border flows.

title: High-Risk Jurisdiction Transfers
text: High-Risk Jurisdiction Transfers (POL-002) - High-Risk Jurisdiction List: For this synthetic bank, the internal high-risk list includes Nigeria (NG) and the Cayman Islands (KY). The list is reviewed quarterly by the Financial Crime Committee.

title: High-Risk Jurisdiction Transfers
text: High-Risk Jurisdiction Transfers (POL-002) - Detection Rules: Rule GEO-R1: any single transfer above INR 20,00,000 to a counterparty in a listed jurisdiction is held for review. Rule GEO-R2: cumulative transfers above INR 50,00,000 to listed jurisdictions within 30 days from one customer also trigger review.

title: High-Risk Jurisdiction Transfers
text: High-Risk Jurisdiction Transfers (POL-002) - Required Controls: Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) is mandatory before release: purpose of payment, relationship to counterparty, source of funds and supporting documents such as invoices or contracts. Release needs written approval from a Compliance Officer.

title: High-Risk Jurisdiction Transfers
text: High-Risk Jurisdiction Transfers (POL-002) - Escalation and SLA: Held transfers must be reviewed within 1 business day. If documents are not supplied within 5 business days, the transfer is rejected and the case is evaluated for STR filing.

title: High-Risk Jurisdiction Transfers
text: High-Risk Jurisdiction Transfers (POL-002) - Exceptions: Pre-approved corporate clients with a documented trade-finance relationship may use a streamlined review, but the transfer must still be logged with its justification.

title: Velocity Monitoring Rule
text: Velocity Monitoring Rule (POL-003) - Purpose and Scope: This rule detects account takeover, mule activity and automated fraud by monitoring the speed of outgoing payments. It applies to UPI, IMPS and NEFT channels.

title: Velocity Monitoring Rule
text: Velocity Monitoring Rule (POL-003) - Detection Rules: Rule VEL-R1: more than 15 outgoing transfers within 60 minutes from one account triggers an automatic temporary hold. Rule VEL-R2: more than 10 transfers of INR 2,000 to INR 9,999 within 30 minutes to different beneficiaries is flagged as a possible mule or scam pattern.

title: Velocity Monitoring Rule
text: Velocity Monitoring Rule (POL-003) - Automated Response: The system places a temporary hold on further outgoing payments and sends an alert to the customer's registered mobile number. The hold lasts up to 24 hours unless released earlier by a fraud analyst.

title: Velocity Monitoring Rule
text: Velocity Monitoring Rule (POL-003) - Analyst Review: The fraud analyst checks device and location changes, new beneficiaries, recent credential changes and the customer's normal activity. Outcomes are: release, confirm fraud and block, or escalate to AML if funds appear to be layered through mule accounts.

title: Velocity Monitoring Rule
text: Velocity Monitoring Rule (POL-003) - Customer Communication: Customers are contacted through verified channels only. Staff must never ask for PINs, OTPs or passwords.

title: KYC Periodic Review Guideline
text: KYC Periodic Review Guideline (REG-001) - Review Frequency: KYC refresh is required every 2 years for high-risk customers, every 8 years for medium-risk customers and every 10 years for low-risk customers, counted from the last verification.

title: KYC Periodic Review Guideline
text: KYC Periodic Review Guideline (REG-001) - Restrictions on Expired KYC: Accounts with expired KYC must be restricted after notice to the customer. Restricted accounts may receive credits but outgoing debits are blocked until KYC is refreshed.

title: KYC Periodic Review Guideline
text: KYC Periodic Review Guideline (REG-001) - Risk Rating Linkage: Customers rated HIGH, and customers with open AML alerts, are prioritised for early refresh. A pending KYC status combined with high-value transactions must be reported to compliance.

title: Enhanced Due Diligence Procedure
text: Enhanced Due Diligence Procedure (POL-004) - When EDD Applies: EDD applies to HIGH risk-rated customers, transactions with high-risk jurisdictions, customers with adverse media, and accounts whose activity departs sharply from their expected profile.

title: Enhanced Due Diligence Procedure
text: Enhanced Due Diligence Procedure (POL-004) - EDD Steps: Verify source of funds and source of wealth, confirm beneficial ownership for non-individual customers, obtain senior management approval, and increase monitoring frequency to monthly.

title: Enhanced Due Diligence Procedure
text: Enhanced Due Diligence Procedure (POL-004) - Documentation: EDD records must show who performed the review, what documents were checked, the outcome and the next review date.

title: Alert Disposition and Case Documentation
text: Alert Disposition and Case Documentation (POL-005) - Disposition Categories: Every alert must be closed as one of: False Positive, Suspicious (escalated), Confirmed Fraud, or Insufficient Information (pending). Each closure needs a written rationale.

title: Alert Disposition and Case Documentation
text: Alert Disposition and Case Documentation (POL-005) - Finding Report Format: A documented finding contains: alert ID, rule triggered, entities involved, supporting transactions, policy clauses cited, risk assessment, recommended action, and reviewer sign-off.

title: Alert Disposition and Case Documentation
text: Alert Disposition and Case Documentation (POL-005) - Audit Trail: All queries, evidence and decisions are time-stamped and attributable to a named user. Audit-ready reports must be reproducible from stored evidence.

title: Alert Disposition and Case Documentation
text: Alert Disposition and Case Documentation (POL-005) - Quality Review: A 10 percent sample of closed alerts is re-reviewed monthly by Compliance QA. Closure without evidence is recorded as a control failure.

title: STR Filing Procedure
text: STR Filing Procedure (POL-006) - Filing Timeline: An STR must be filed with the Financial Intelligence Unit within 7 working days of the Principal Officer concluding that the activity is suspicious. Attempted transactions are also reportable.

title: STR Filing Procedure
text: STR Filing Procedure (POL-006) - STR Contents: Include customer identifiers, account numbers, transaction details, red flags observed, the grounds for suspicion and supporting documents. Narrative must be factual and specific.

title: STR Filing Procedure
text: STR Filing Procedure (POL-006) - Post-Filing: Continue monitoring the account, apply additional controls if required, and review whether the customer relationship should continue. No tipping-off.

title: Record Retention and Reporting Requirements
text: Record Retention and Reporting Requirements (REG-002) - Retention Periods: Transaction records and customer identification records are retained for at least 5 years after the transaction or the end of the business relationship, whichever is later.

title: Record Retention and Reporting Requirements
text: Record Retention and Reporting Requirements (REG-002) - Cash Transaction Reporting: Cash transactions above INR 10,00,000, and integrally connected series of cash transactions within a month, are reported to the FIU by the 15th of the following month.

title: Liquidity Risk Monitoring (LCR)
text: Liquidity Risk Monitoring (LCR) (POL-007) - Liquidity Coverage Ratio Floor: The bank maintains a Liquidity Coverage Ratio of at least 100 percent, computed as high-quality liquid assets divided by net cash outflows over 30 days. An internal early-warning trigger is set at 110 percent.

title: Liquidity Risk Monitoring (LCR)
text: Liquidity Risk Monitoring (LCR) (POL-007) - Escalation: A breach of the early-warning trigger is reported to the ALCO within 1 business day. A breach below 100 percent requires an immediate remediation plan and regulatory notification.
